boundary_rationale: The unit opens where the geographic scene turns from darkened lands into light: “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish.” (web:Isa.9.1 = oshb:Isa.8.23). A chain of causal ki-clauses then carries the same argument forward without a fresh subject or addressee — the broken yoke, the burned battle gear, and finally the birth announcement all answer the same reason as the opening light and the multiplied joy — so the whole span is read as one syntactically continuous declaration rather than split at any internal ki-boundary. The throne-naming clause reads פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖ד שַׂר שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier), rendered “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5); an OSHB exegesis note sits at this same verse (oshb:Isa.9.5), single-witness apparatus only, never text bytes, and is disclosed rather than argued as content. The unit closes at the government-increase clause, which the letter bytes stage as a doubled ketiv/qere token pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה (oshb:Isa.9.6, byte tier) — the ketiv form carries a final mem in medial position; the quote engages both staged forms, not one alone — rendered “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6). No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the light-dawning announcement from the throne-naming and its government clause is rejected because the chain of coordinated ki-clauses keeps both halves inside one argument for the nation's joy.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A Masoretic setumah break follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, for a close already argued from the ki-chain and the fresh subject at web:Isa.9.8; it is never treated as the driver. A ketiv/qere note also sits at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), inside this unit's own span; it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading. The medial final-mem in the doubled token is letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg of any size. The referent of the throne names (a court style exalting a Davidic king, versus a fuller messianic reading) is not settled by this boundary decision and is held open.

boundary_rationale: A fresh declarative sentence with a new grammatical subject opens the unit: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב (oshb:Isa.9.7, byte tier), “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.” (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7); Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit. The unit closes at the refrain bracket בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11, byte tier), “For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.12 = oshb:Isa.9.11).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this stanza through the next refrain occurrence is rejected because the following material renews the indictment with fresh content rather than continuing the same clause. A larger rival reads the whole judgment sequence as one continuous poem opening already at web:Isa.5.25 (the refrain recurs across five verses; sweep: 5 verses), with this stanza as a later movement rather than a fresh onset.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

The closing refrain recurs byte-identically at five sites across the book (sweep: 5 verses), earliest at web:Isa.5.25, and on that basis a rival architecture reads the whole run from there as one continuous poem rather than granting this stanza its own bracket — disclosed rather than adopted.

boundary_rationale: No fresh subject or addressee reopens after the preceding refrain; the unit continues the same indictment before closing at its own refrain occurrence, בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.16, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.17 = oshb:Isa.9.16).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this stanza as the poem's opening unit is rejected because its own onset carries no fresh subject or addressee, but a continuation of the preceding judgment. The same refrain closes web:Isa.5.25 as well as the other stanza-ends in this run (sweep: 5 verses), so a rival reading folds every stanza back into one long poem beginning there instead of granting this one a separate boundary.

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark falls inside this unit's own span, at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13); tier-3, single-witness, disclosed as an interior break that does not relocate the refrain-marked close. boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a fresh image continuing the same judgment voice, “For wickedness burns like a fire.” (web:Isa.9.18 = oshb:Isa.9.17), and closes at its own refrain occurrence: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.20, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.21 = oshb:Isa.9.20).

The refrain's five occurrences (sweep: 5 verses) start at web:Isa.5.25 and support a rival view that the entire sequence is one interrupted poem rather than four bracketed stanzas.

Because the same byte-level refrain also closes web:Isa.5.25 and its other three sites (sweep: 5 verses), a rival architecture folds this stanza into one long poem beginning there rather than granting it an independent boundary — disclosed rather than adopted.

boundary_rationale: A woe-onset opens the unit with a named class of offenders distinct from the nation addressed in the preceding stanzas: ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.10.1, byte tier), “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees” (web:Isa.10.1). The unit nonetheless closes at the same refrain bracket as the three preceding stanzas: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.10.4, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.10.4).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this stanza as an ordinary member of the surrounding woe-oracle series addressed to Assyria is rejected because its refrain reproduces the three prior stanzas' closing bytes (sweep: 3 verses) and its own target is the unnamed decree-writers, not Assyria. A rival architecture nonetheless reads the whole refrain-bracketed run as one poem rather than as this stanza's independent unit.

device_notes: This unit carries both a formal woe-onset and the refrain-closed stanza pattern of the surrounding judgment poem; it is tagged for the onset it actually carries in its own bytes, with the refrain-poem membership disclosed as texture rather than folded into the type label. boundary_rationale: A new woe-onset addresses a wholly different subject — Assyria, not the decree-writers of the preceding unit: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט (oshb:Isa.10.5, byte tier), “Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!” (web:Isa.10.5). The unit runs through Assyria's own boastful self-assessment and closes at the rhetorical question comparing Jerusalem to Samaria, “shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?” (web:Isa.10.11), before a fresh temporal-response clause opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the king's boast quotation that follows is rejected because a temporal-response clause opens a distinct divine reply rather than continuing Assyria's own self-description.

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.4 and another closes this one at web:Isa.10.11; both tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the boundary is argued from the addressee shift and the response clause that follows, not from the marks.

boundary_rationale: A temporal-response formula opens the divine reply to Assyria's arrogance: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע (oshb:Isa.10.12, byte tier), “Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his arrogant looks.” (web:Isa.10.12). A further therefore-clause לָ֠כֵן (oshb:Isa.10.16, byte tier) restates the same sentence rather than opening a new addressee, and the unit closes with the forest stripped bare, “The remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child could write their number.” (web:Isa.10.19).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the two therefore-clauses at web:Isa.10.12 and web:Isa.10.16 as separate rows is rejected because both continue one uninterrupted divine response to the same quoted boast, with no addressee change between them.
literature_type_guess: judgment speech answering the instrument's boast

device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.11 and a petuchah mark closes this one at web:Isa.10.19; both tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the internal therefore-clause at web:Isa.10.16 is treated as continuing the same speech rather than as a further seam, since no addressee change accompanies it. The forest imagery that closes this unit carries the same root swept as a remnant object elsewhere in this stretch; here it functions as a plain common noun, a different object from the name-reactivating clauses argued in the unit that follows.

boundary_rationale: A formulaic 'in that day' onset opens the unit with the remnant of Israel as its subject: וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier), “It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on him who struck them, but shall lean on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.” (web:Isa.10.20). The reactivating clause שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.10.21, byte tier) restates the son's sign-name given at web:Isa.7.3, “A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.” (web:Isa.10.21); the unit closes with the severity coda, “For the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will make a full end, and that determined, throughout all the earth.” (web:Isa.10.23), before a distinct divine-word formula opens the following unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading only the return of the remnant (web:Isa.10.20-web:Isa.10.21) as the bounded unit is rejected because the full-end clause that follows shares the same 'in that day' frame and the same remnant vocabulary rather than opening independently.
literature_type_guess: remnant-return oracle with a judgment coda

A petuchah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.10.19 and a setumah mark closes this one at web:Isa.10.23; both tier-3, single-witness.

boundary_rationale: A divine messenger formula opens the unit: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, says,” (web:Isa.10.24), addressed directly to Zion rather than continuing the third-person remnant announcement of the preceding unit. The unit closes with the promised relief, “It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.” (web:Isa.10.27), before the scene shifts to the march narrative that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the assurance oracle through the march description that follows is rejected because that description opens with a fresh narrative scene rather than continuing the same divine-word formula.

boundary_rationale: A new poetic movement traces the invader's approach by named place: בָּ֥א עַל עַיַּ֖ת (oshb:Isa.10.28, byte tier), “He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.” (web:Isa.10.28). The same scene resolves in a behold-formula naming the divine response: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier), “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.” (web:Isa.10.33); the unit closes with the felled forest, “He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.” (web:Isa.10.34).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the felling of the forest at web:Isa.10.33 from the march narrative that precedes it is rejected because the behold-clause resolves the same approaching-army scene rather than opening an unrelated one.

boundary_rationale: A new subject enters on the felled forest's own image: וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier), “A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.” (web:Isa.11.1); the stock/stump imagery deliberately answers the felled trees of the preceding unit. The unit closes with the peaceable-kingdom inclusio, “the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.” (web:Isa.11.9), before a further 'in that day' formula opens the next unit on the same figure.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through the following verse is rejected because that verse restarts with its own 'in that day' formula naming a further, distinct action rather than continuing the same clause.

boundary_rationale: A formulaic onset restarts the Jesse figure as an ensign to the nations rather than continuing the peaceable-kingdom description: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier), “It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.” (web:Isa.11.10). The following verse marks its own action as explicit repetition — יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), “the Lord will set his hand again the second time” (web:Isa.11.11) — distinguishing that regathering act from the nations-seeking-the-root act named here, which argues for a boundary between them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the following regathering oracle is rejected because that oracle explicitly marks its own action as happening 'again the second time,' distinguishing it from the action named here.

device_notes: A petuchah mark closes the preceding unit at web:Isa.11.9, and the same mark type falls again at this unit's own verse, web:Isa.11.10 — the more emphatic of the two Masoretic paragraph-break types, tier-3, single-witness, corroborating rather than driving the boundary already argued from the formula and the second-time marker. Whether this verse is better read as the closing coda of the preceding shoot-of-Jesse unit, as its own bridge, or as the opening of the regathering oracle that follows is not fully settled; the boundary drawn here is the held, honestly-medium_low position.

boundary_rationale: The second-time marker opens a distinct regathering action: יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), “It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11). The unit closes on the second-exodus echo, “There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.” (web:Isa.11.16), at the chapter's own close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the regathering promise into a Judah/Ephraim reconciliation unit and a separate highway unit is rejected because both remain governed by the same 'in that day' onset with no intervening addressee shift.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens the chapter-bounded thanksgiving hymn with its first strophe: “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.1), and its own doubled divine name יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier), “for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song” (web:Isa.12.2). A second strophe restates the same onset formula (sweep: 2 verses) rather than opening a new addressee: “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.4), and the unit closes at the chapter's own end, “for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!” (web:Isa.12.6).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the hymn at its second 'you will say' onset into two separate rows is rejected because both strophes share the same speaker, addressee, and doxological register within one chapter-bounded unit.

device_notes: A petuchah mark closes this unit at its own final verse, web:Isa.12.6; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the close is already fixed by the frame boundary carried forward from the larger architecture. The twin 'in that day you will say' onsets (sweep: 2 verses) at web:Isa.12.1 and web:Isa.12.4 read the same in the English rendering and share the same underlying bayom-hahu formula even though the verb of speaking differs in person and number; both strophes are kept inside one hymn rather than split, since neither addressee nor register changes between them. The Yah-plus-tetragrammaton stack at web:Isa.12.2 is counted as its own short-form site, never blended into the plain tetragrammaton census.
